assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into a controllable light-matter platform: strong coupling of a single microwave photon to an artificial atom, dispersive readout, and the architecture that underlies essentially every superconducting quantum processor. The idea is original, clear and has had very large lasting impact across quantum optics and quantum information. From my subject-matter vantage this is the most consequential circuit-level development after the macroscopic-tunnelling work.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al., Schoelkopf group) split between theory and experiment. A fair three-person configuration is Schoelkopf and Wallraff for the experimental realisation and Girvin for the Yale theory leadership; Blais, a principal theory author, is the hardest omission and the choice between Girvin and Blais is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups for two decades, interpretation stable, with dispersive readout, bosonic codes and multi-qubit processors built on it. Recognition would be timely and not premature, though the very recent 2025 prize in the same broad area could argue for a pause.
uncertainties: Choice among four credited theorists/experimentalists limited to three; Girvin versus Blais is disputed on credit.
Close thematic proximity to the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize and to my own field; I cannot independently verify how the committee weighs back-to-back recognition of related work.
Detailed priority between theory proposal and first experiment is from memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials: theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle, then observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity. It created a new field with tunable strongly correlated physics and wide impact, and it is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments. This maps naturally onto a three-person theory plus experiment prize. Cory Dean, Kim and others also contributed to moire platforms, and Cao as lead author is not credited here, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups worldwide, but the origin of superconductivity and the full phase diagram are still debated; the field is young (about eight years), so recognition may be somewhat early though momentum is strong.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity remains unsettled.
Broader moire field credit (other platforms, earlier theory such as Lopes dos Santos) may complicate a clean attribution.
Whether the committee views this as mature enough is a timing question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum computer and quantum simulation with cold atoms; ion-trap experiments (Blatt and others) implemented gates, entanglement and small algorithms. This is foundational for quantum information processing and is central to the quantum-computing programme that I know well.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators (1995 ion-trap gate proposal). Blatt is a leading experimental realiser, though Wineland (recognised in 2012) and Monroe/Wineland-group NIST demonstrations of the first gate are an overlap and credit question. The configuration is plausible but not uniquely settled.
assessment.maturity: Roughly three decades of confirmation and now commercial platforms, so it is mature. Partial overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland) lowers novelty margin.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize and with NIST/Innsbruck priority for the first gate.
Zoller also appears on the optical-lattice candidate, so credit across the quantum-simulation entries could interact.
Whether Monroe or Wineland-group members should be included is not resolved within the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 founded quantum cryptography, grounding secure key distribution in quantum mechanics and in Bell-type reasoning. It is original, conceptually clear and has produced a large experimental and technological field.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is independent in formulation. A three-person prize is natural, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not on the list and Zeilinger's related experiments were recognised in 2022.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally mature (fibre and satellite QKD) and long established; recognition is overdue rather than premature. Practical security issues are engineering questions, not doubts about the underlying discovery.
uncertainties: Wiesner's priority for conjugate coding is outside the credited names.
Overlap with the 2022 prize for entanglement and Bell tests.
Whether the committee regards it as physics rather than information theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping proposed by Katori, delivers clock instability and accuracy of order 1e-18 and enables new tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear, high-impact step in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength idea; Ye's group built the most precise lattice clocks and pushed the performance record. A two-person prize is clean, though Ludlow, Lemonde and others contributed and the ion-clock lineage overlaps with earlier prizes (Hall, Haensch, Wineland).
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks (Sr, Yb) confirm the performance, and redefinition of the second is under discussion; the field is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock-related prizes (2005, 2012) may reduce novelty.
Thorium-229 and ion clocks are competing frontiers that could recast priorities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson confirmed the mechanism of mass in the Standard Model and was among the largest scientific achievements of the era. Impact and clarity are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory. Credit for the experiment is diffuse across thousands, so the three credited founding spokespeople (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are a defensible but imperfect proxy; the statutes' three-person limit makes this the main obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by two experiments and by Run 2 couplings. The only maturity concern is that the prize for the theory has already been given and the allocation problem for collaborations is acute.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit cannot be fairly captured by three individuals.
Founding spokespersons versus analysts and detector builders is disputed.
Outside my specialty; I rely on general knowledge of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators created a major field of topological quantum matter, with an experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells. Impact on condensed-matter theory and materials is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory; Molenkamp's group with Zhang and collaborators provided the first experimental demonstration. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (predicting HgTe) and the 3D-TI contributions complicate credit; the supplied names give a coherent two-theory plus one-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many materials and ARPES, and the concept is stable, though it is partly adjacent to the 2016 topology prize. Recognition would be timely but with some novelty overlap.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and 3D TIs is outside this credit set.
Partial thematic overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize.
Applications have been slower than early expectations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault-tolerant codes showed that large quantum computers are possible in principle despite noise; Shor's code and the stabilizer and surface or toric code lineage are the basis for today's error-correction experiments. For the field I work in, this theoretical foundation is crucial.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently produced the first quantum codes in 1995 to 1996, while Kitaev introduced topological codes and fault tolerance. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others are not credited, so allocation is contested. The three names form a plausible prize but leave visible omissions.
assessment.maturity: Increasingly validated by recent below-threshold experiments, but a full fault-tolerant machine does not yet exist, so recognition might still be early. The theory itself is long settled.
uncertainties: Many equally important contributors (Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill, Laflamme) are not in the credited set.
Experimental demonstration of scalable logical qubits is recent and incomplete.
Kitaev also appears under topological superconductivity, a possible credit overlap.
